raw_answer_text:
A1: To every station on the segment — it is broadcast as an Ethernet broadcast frame.
A2: It lacks a mapping between the target host's IP (protocol) address and its hardware (MAC) address in its ARP cache/table.
A3: It stores the sender's protocol (IP) address together with the sender's hardware (MAC) address.
A4: No, only the intended target host responds; other hosts silently discard or merely note the broadcast.
A5: It is sent directly (unicast) to the requesting host, not broadcast.
A6: It caches/updates the mapping of the target's protocol address to its hardware address in its ARP table, completing the resolution.
A7: The requesting host does not know the target's hardware address; obtaining it is the purpose of the request.
A8: The merge of the sender's address mapping into its own table happens before it checks whether the packet is a request or a reply.
